messages:
customer-ops (AcmePay): Hey team — since 07:20 UTC our integrations to Redwood hosted inference are intermittently returning 502/504s and timeouts. Customer sees ~3-5% error rate, spike when traffic peaks. Errors show up as TLS handshake timeout / upstream reset in our proxy logs. :rotating_light:

amanda (support): Thanks — can you paste a sample request-id and the exact error body/headers? Also which region/model?

customer-ops (AcmePay): request-id=rid_0a1b2c3d4e, endpoint=/v1/generate, region=us-west-2, model=redwood-v1. Payloads are small plaintext prompts. Error body: 502 Bad Gateway. Our edge logs show: 
```
upstream response timeout while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.14, server: api.redwood.example, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.20.30.40:8080/", host: "api.redwood.example"
```
We also saw TLS handshake timeouts from our side to api.redwood.example: "TLS handshake timed out after 5s"

liam (sre): Copying in eng-infra. Two quick checks: 1) Any recent cert rotation or CA changes? 2) Are you using a custom resolver or private DNS?

customer-ops (AcmePay): No cert changes on our side. We do use an internal resolver that forwards to 10.100.100.10 (corporate).

deploy-bot: deploy/redwood-edge-cert-rotation started at 07:15 UTC, id=deploy-2026-03-15-0715, status=rolling

amanda (support): Hmm — deploy-bot indicates a cert rotation started ~07:15, that lines up. Could be in-flight cert chain propagation + resolver TTL causing mixed certs leading to occasional handshake failures.

jess (network): Can you run a quick dig and curl from affected host? Example commands: 
```
dig +short api.redwood.example @10.100.100.10
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:34.201.12.45 https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```

customer-ops (AcmePay): dig output intermittently returns two IPs, sometimes blank (SERVFAIL). Sample: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example @10.100.100.10
34.201.12.45

# then after ~10s

; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> api.redwood.example @10.100.100.10
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 2, ADDITIONAL: 1
```
And curl sometimes fails with: 
```
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5001 milliseconds
```

nate (eng-infra): Ok that SERVFAIL is suspicious. If their resolver occasionally returns SERVFAIL during rotation, clients will hit different edge nodes with different certs. Two parallel problems: DNS instability + cert rollout timing. We'll escalate to infra.

liam (sre): Action items: 
1) Support to give customer a short mitigation: change resolver to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 temporarily (to avoid corporate forwarder) and confirm error rate drops.
2) Eng-infra to check cert rollout state and revert or pause if some edge nodes still present old cert chain.
3) Collect pcap + TLS debug on customer side for correlation id rid_0a1b2c3d4e. Use: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/redwood-rid0a.pcap host 34.201.12.45 and port 443`

amanda (support): Customer confirms switching to 1.1.1.1 reduced errors to ~0.2% within 3 minutes. So likely DNS flakiness. They can't permanently change resolver but will keep it as short-lived test. :thumbsup:

nate (eng-infra): We see in deployment logs that cert rotation completed, but a small subset of edge nodes reported reload errors and retried with an incomplete chain between 07:14:30–07:22:10 UTC. Those nodes also had TTL=30 on DNS records in our CDN edge config; the corporate forwarder cached negative responses. We're going to: 
- Immediately push a forced reload/clear on the 6 affected nodes.
- Extend DNS TTL temporarily to 300 while the rollout stabilizes.
- Add monitoring for SERVFAIL spikes from external resolvers.

jess (network): Recommend adding a short-term mitigation in the console: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and 2s longer connect timeout when TLS handshake failures exceed threshold, to reduce 502 surface for customers. We can prototype a per-customer policy.

amanda (support): I told AcmePay we'll credit the affected tokens for the window 07:15–07:25 and will notify when the fix is fully validated. They asked for repro steps so their security team can audit — included tcpdump and curl outputs.

liam (sre): Next steps for escalation: I'll open an incident ticket and tag eng-runtime and eng-infra, with SLA P2. Incident summary: intermittent 502/504 due to mixed cert chain + upstream DNS SERVFAIL from corporate forwarders during cert rotation. Attachments: deploy logs, affected node IDs, customer pcap, DNS query logs.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created by liam (sre) at 07:45 UTC — severity P2, assignees: nate, jess, liam.

customer-ops (AcmePay): Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Please ping when nodes are cleared and we’ll re-run full traffic tests.

amanda (support): Will follow up once eng confirms forced reloads and DNS TTL bump. Marking as in-progress. :white_check_mark:
